title: Zone-granular quota slices and deferred eviction protocol for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement zone-granular throughput quota slices and a deferred eviction protocol to provide predictable throughput guarantees for regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets while preserving data residency constraints and improving graceful failover behavior.

Context: Enterprise customers reserve dedicated capacity across a region (multiple AZs). Today we allocate capacity at the region level which can cause aggressive cross-zone eviction and immediate traffic migration during drains or failures. That results in transient overloading of surviving zones, SLO violations, and opaque customer-facing behavior.

Proposal summary:
1) Quota slices: allocate each dedicated commitment a set of zone-granular quota slices (e.g., 3 slices for a 3-AZ region). Slices are weighted based on committed throughput and zone affinity tags. Slices act as admission tokens that gate request admission into zone-local pools.
2) Deferred eviction protocol: when a zone signals an eviction/drain, instead of immediate forced rehoming, the protocol marks the origin slice as "deferred-eviction" and opens a short soft-drain window (configurable: default 60s). During the window the system attempts to shed non-SLA traffic, apply traffic shaping, prewarm target slices, and only escalate to hard eviction if soft-mitigations fail.
3) Admission controller changes: extend the dedicated admission controller to be zone-aware, consume slice tokens, and support emergency overflow lanes with strict cost/latency tiering and audit logs for cross-zone moves.
4) Residency guardrail: attach residency labels to slices. Slices for data-sovereign commitments are non-transferable across jurisdictions; attempts to overflow to disallowed zones will be rejected and trigger customer-facing alerting and operator playbook steps.
5) Autoscaling interplay: autoscale decisions will be slice-aware. We will introduce a concept of zone-level reserve buffer (a percent of slice capacity) that autoscaler can ramp into before global scale-up to minimize cross-zone rehoming.

Why this matters: Reduces blast radius when a zone degrades, preserves predictable per-customer throughput for committed contracts, and respects data residency constraints while giving operators levers to manage graceful degradation instead of immediate hard evictions.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement billing changes for partial slice usage, nor does it change public API surface for customers beyond optional placement hints. Billing/contract logic to be addressed in PM follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Regionally reserved dedicated commitments can be decomposed into N zone-granular quota slices and stored in the commitment metadata.
Admission controller consumes zone slice tokens and rejects admission when the corresponding slice is exhausted unless overflow lane is explicitly allowed by the commitment.
Deferred eviction flow executes soft-drain mitigations (60s default) before hard evict and logs actions to audit trail.
Residency-protected slices cannot be migrated to a zone outside the allowed jurisdiction; attempted migrations produce operator alerts and a documented runbook trigger.
Autoscaler respects zone reserve buffers and prefers local buffer exhaustion before initiating cross-zone scale-up or hard eviction.

SLA test: Under a simulated single-AZ outage, 90% of committed throughput is preserved with p99 tail latency increase < 2x for affected customers in the soft-drain window, and no silent cross-jurisdiction migrations occur.
E2E tests and canary rollout validate the protocol on an internal dedicated pool and include dashboards for slice utilization and eviction events.
notes: Trade-offs: adding slice bookkeeping increases control plane metadata. We minimize impact by making slices lightweight references rather than duplicative allocations.
We prefer a soft-drain window to give us time to prewarm and shed best-effort traffic; the default 60s is tunable per-contract and must be surfaced in operator config.
Fallback: commitments without zone affinity will use a default weighted-slice strategy based on historical usage distribution.
Risk: misconfigured overflow lanes could concentrate traffic and risk cascading failures; we will gate overflow lanes via policy and limit QPS/weight.
